content:
In June this year, we reported three cases of apps from US-sanctioned Russian banks disguising themselves to slip into the App Store. Two months later, another example has reached the top of the iPhone App Store.

K8CHEN PRO is the latest such case. Its App Store listing masquerades the app as a kitchen design tool with augmented reality (AR) features.

Once you open the app, the disguise quickly falls apart. The privacy policy link is set on the App Store page, and states that it was auto-generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — itself probably a red flag.

Regardless, this app is unmistakably a client app for T-Bank. What puzzles me is that apps like these can keep getting through App Store review.

When they hit the App Store charts because everyone knows about them, anyone with eyes can see they're not the kind of apps that should be listed. It really makes you wonder.

For the other cases reported in June, see here and here.

Update: Sure enough, the app has now been removed from the App Store.
